doc_screened_files.reason: Top stack frame is `rustc_mir_transform::inline::Inliner::try_inlining`, and the ICE only appears with `-Zinline-mir=yes` during `optimized_mir` for `field_array`. This strongly points to MIR inlining corrupting caller/callee MIR state, likely around remapping locals/places/blocks for this invalid impl method body.

The panic site is directly `compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/tcx.rs:131:61` with an index-out-of-bounds while computing MIR semantic helper logic over places/operands/rvalues. That suggests inliner-produced MIR references an invalid local/place projection and this file is where the bad index is dereferenced.

Less direct than `inline.rs`, but this is another MIR-cloning/remapping-heavy transform in the same crate. The bug shape is an out-of-bounds local index after body rewriting, so files that synthesize/remap MIR bodies are globally suspicious.

Shim construction also creates and rewrites synthetic MIR bodies, similar to inlining’s remapping hazards. Since the issue labels include instance-resolution and the failure occurs while obtaining optimized instance MIR, synthetic-body handling is a plausible contributing site.

This file defines shared MIR body/location/local infrastructure used throughout analysis and transforms. An index-out-of-bounds on MIR locals during inlining can stem from violated MIR body invariants maintained or assumed here.

The reproducer uses destructuring assignment to a tuple-struct field pattern (`Foo([a, b]) = ...`), so statement/place/rvalue helper logic around assignments is relevant. If inlining rewrites or inspects such statements incorrectly, this helper layer is a likely participant.

The crash is reproduced with `-Zvalidate-mir`, and this pass owns MIR invariant checking. Even if not root cause, its phase-specific assumptions may interact with malformed MIR from inlining and help localize the invariant being violated.

The source trigger is a destructuring assignment with nested aggregate pattern shape. MIR building for pattern-like assignment lowering happens here, so malformed initial MIR for destructuring could later be mishandled by the inliner.

The reproducer intentionally contains an invalid trait impl method signature (`default(&mut self)` for `Default`). The issue labels include `F-compare-impl-item` and `F-trait-impl-signature-mismatch`; if impl-item compatibility checking leaves behind a bad body/signature state that still reaches MIR optimization, this file is an upstream root-cause candidate.

The failing call is `Default::default()` on a type whose impl method signature mismatches the trait. Instance/callee confirmation for method/associated item calls is therefore relevant, especially given the issue labels mention instance resolution and impl-item signature mismatch.
